newsitem.title: spain: SOCCER-ESPANYOL SIGN OLD BOY RADUCIOIU AND WILD BOY OLMETA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ESPANYOL SIGN OLD BOY RADUCIOIU AND WILD BOY OLMETA.

text.p: Romanian international forward Florin Raducioiu and hot-headed French goalkeeper Pascal Olmeta signed for Espanyol on Wednesday ending unhappy spells at West Ham and Lyon respectively.

Olmeta was dismissed by Lyon last week after punching a team mate, while Raducioiu's move to England ended in relative failure with just a handful of appearances for the London club and only two goals.
Raducioiu was expected back in Barcelona on Thursday after settling his affairs in England but because of fog delays in England he might not be able to start training back with Espanyol until Friday.

It was reported he had signed a two-and-a-half year contract worth 400,000 pounds ($668,000) a year and the 27-year-old was expected to go straight into the side for Monday's home league match against Sevilla.

Raducioiu's return to Espanyol where he scored 14 goals in 38 appearances in the last two seasons, means that West Ham can now step up their bid for Celtic's unsettled Dutch striker Pierre Van Hooydonk.

Raducioiu cost 2.4 million pounds ($4 million) when he moved from the Spanish club in the summer, but it is believed West Ham recieved only 1.4 million pounds ($2.3 million) from Espanyol for his return.

The arrival of Olmeta is likely to end speculation that Espanyol would replace injured 'keeper Toni Jimenez with Real Madrid veteran Paco Buyo, who has lost his place since the arrival of former German international Bodo Illgner.

Olmeta was sacked by Lyon earlier this month for punching a team mate at the end of Lyon's 1-0 home defeat to Nantes in December. The hot-tempered veteran twice punched defender Jean-Luc Sassus who suffered concussion as a result of the blows.

But Espanyol have decided to release Pepe Carcelen, the coach whose resignation on Monday gave way to the reappointment of Vicente Miera. Carcelen had been expected to return to his job as deputy first-team coach

On the day when the Spanish winter transfer window closed, Celta Vigo confirmed the purchase of Moises Garcia from Leganes after talks between the second division's leading goalscorer and English club Sheffield Wednesday broke down.
